reason: The two are almost identical. Each shrinks the bedroom photo to a small thumbnail in the left corner. The white heart/cross shape that held the copy is lost, and only a faint stray arc is left near 'Silk Linen' / the URL (slightly higher in A, slightly lower in B). The three-line headline is small and stacked as in a square layout instead of reading across a leaderboard. The right ~40% of the banner is dead white space. The URL is tiny. Neither has a clear focal point or uses the banner shape.

Both lose the main barrel photo, which shrinks to a tiny thumbnail at the bottom, and the triangle logo becomes a speck beside it. The small em-dash divider is blown up into a thick black bar across the canvas. Around these, huge empty white areas leave the design unrecognisable. A spaces the tagline, thumbnail and logo slightly more evenly. B jams the tagline right on top of the thumbnail and logo, and it is otherwise the same failure.

A is basically the square shrunk into a band across the middle of the tall canvas. There's dead blue space above the yellow bar and below the doctor, whose body ends in a hard straight edge in mid-canvas. The symptom list and the yellow call-to-action are too small to read, and there's a big empty gap under the headline. B actually rearranges the layout to read top to bottom, with a large headline, a readable list and a full-width call-to-action, but it has clear flaws. The '6' sits alone on its own line. The list wraps so that 'Sore throat Headache' runs together on one line. The doctor no longer runs off the canvas edge: his body is cut off with hard edges at the left and bottom, so he looks like a cropped box. The hashtag bar is inset instead of spanning the full width.

Both share the same flaws. The red panel's lower ~40% is empty dead space under the attribution. The skyline no longer overlaps the red panel as it did in the original, and floats in a separate white band. The decorative tick lines and grey background stripes look arbitrary. A keeps the skyline full-bleed and anchored to the bottom, like the original. B shrinks it into a hard-edged rectangle with visibly clipped left and right ends, floating above the card's bottom edge with a white gap below, so it reads as a pasted-in crop.

A: the lightbulb and question-mark doodles are drawn straight onto the boy's nose and cheek, an unwanted collision that defaces the hero photo. The arrow doodle is clipped at the left edge, and the face crop is so tight and blurry that the shoulders and backpack are gone. The headline is at least a reasonable size. B: the doodles stay off the face, but the headline/subtitle block is tiny for the banner and floats in a wide empty field. The molecule is shrunk and jammed against the right edge, the arrow is clipped at the left edge, and the same blurry face crop leaves weak hierarchy overall. B is the less damaging of the two because nothing collides with the face.

Both use the same layout. The 'THE US VIDEO GAMES' headline runs right up against the 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL' column. The pink subhead breaks awkwardly, leaving 'CANNOT' alone on its own line. The 3-day-event body copy is too small to read. The symbol row is jammed against the top edge, and the right column is a cramped stack. In B the body copy is squeezed even smaller and crowds against 'BECOME REAL.' with uneven letter spacing, so A is slightly less broken.

Both are the same cramped leaderboard: tiny shape logo, the body copy and URL in the right column are too small to read, 'IN NY.' is orphaned on its own line, and 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL' is squeezed into a narrow four-line stack. A's pink subhead also breaks badly, leaving 'CANNOT' alone on a line. B is worse: the same subhead runs to five lines with 'YOU CANNOT' and 'VIRTUAL' isolated, and it nearly touches the top and bottom edges of the canvas.

Both are unusable. Each puts the forest art in a narrow strip in the middle of a mostly white banner. The headline, subhead, quote and URL are gone, and the only visible text is a tiny, low-contrast 'March 21' in pale yellow on white plus faint stray rules at the left. A also shows a cut-off fragment 'Joint' over the art, which shows the copy was truncated. B shows no copy at all on the art. Neither keeps the message or the hierarchy, and neither fits the banner format.

Both are the same shrunk copy for the skyscraper format: the headline is small and set in a lighter weight than the original, and the cat illustration floats mid-canvas instead of sitting on the bottom edge as it does in the original. That leaves large dead purple bands above and below. A is a little better balanced vertically; B pushes the group higher and leaves an even bigger empty block (about 180px) at the bottom, so it looks top-heavy.

A: hierarchy is inverted. 'food & drinks' is now far bigger than the shrunken 'Order online' headline and runs onto the kraft box, and the two rules no longer line up with the text block, so they float off to the left. B has the same inverted hierarchy and gets worse: the headline is pushed right against the cup, 'food & drinks' runs further across the box and almost touches the bottom rule, and a large dead gap opens between the headline and the subtitle.

A breaks the lockup apart: 'food & drinks' floats near the top, while the 'Order online' headline sits small near the bottom, below its own subline. That inverts the reading order and leaves a huge empty middle, and the rules are stranded at the canvas edges. B keeps the text grouped in the centre, but the headline has shrunk to about subline size, so the hierarchy is lost. The subline also sits above the headline, the rules are detached at the top and bottom edges far from the text, and the cropped image is oversized and pushed off the right edge.

Both reverse the hierarchy: the subline 'food & drinks' is set much larger than the 'Order online' headline. Both also jam the stacked headline against the top and bottom edges of the 50 px strip and crop the product photo to unreadable box fragments. A drops the rules above and below the headline and its 'Order' nearly touches the top edge. B keeps the rules, which is a little more faithful to the original, but they sit right at the canvas edges, so B is only marginally less bad.

A reads left to right: the headline is on the left and the blue and dark info boxes sit side by side on the right, so it stays faithful to the original. Its flaws are that the body copy in both boxes is very small at 90 px tall, the headline sits on a busy photo, and the boxes are crammed against the right edge. B shrinks both info boxes to unreadable micro-text and pushes them into the bottom-left corner in reversed order (dark box before blue), which puts fine print in the lead spot, breaks the reading order and leaves the left side lopsided.

Both use the same enlarged three-line headline over the busy interior photo. It reads well, but it has no backing panel, the dark lamp fragment on the left edge crowds the 'C', and the right third of the canvas is dead space. A joins the blue and black info boxes into one band aligned to the headline's left edge, which keeps them grouped like the original's stacked panels, though the band stops short at about two-thirds of the width. B splits the boxes with an arbitrary gap, and the black box lines up with neither the headline's right edge nor the canvas, so the two boxes look scattered rather than grouped.

A keeps the 'HOHOHO / AGENCY' name order, but the two words are far apart. 'Office Secret Santa' is pushed to the right and jammed against the clipped blue half-ring. The top decoration strip is a jumble of cut-off fragments, and there is dead space at the top and bottom. B groups the text cleanly, but it breaks the brand name: 'HOHOHO' sits below the tagline as an orphaned third line. The ring is clipped flat and the bottom strip is again a row of cut-off fragments, so the fidelity loss tips it slightly below A.

A keeps 'When Life Is Rough / PRAY' as a tight stacked pair, but the divider is scaled into a thick, blurry bar, and the right side breaks the parallel structure: it sets 'When Life Is Great PRAY' on one line with an oversized PRAY at a different height from the left block, and the text is small for the canvas. B's divider is cleaner, but it pulls both phrases apart: 'Rough' floats far above its PRAY, and 'Great' sits a wide gap away from a larger PRAY. That leaves four disconnected fragments with uneven baselines and mismatched PRAY sizes, which is worse grouping than A's.

Both break the original's parallel two-couplet structure: the first 'PRAY' is shoved to the right of 'When Life Is Rough' at a small size while the second 'PRAY' is huge, so the two halves no longer match. The divider is now a vertical rule running beside the 'Great' text instead of separating the two couplets, and the copy sizes are inconsistent. A is marginally better because 'When Life Is Great' sits close to its 'PRAY'. In B, 'Great' floats mid-line with a dead gap above the bottom 'PRAY', which splits that pair apart.

A: the headline is broken into 'CONS TRUC TION' with gaps, so it reads as three fragments. The $14.99 price is stranded under the headline, far from its 'Buy 2 only for' line, which breaks the reading order. The brick is a tiny smudge, and all the copy is very small. B has the same broken headline, plus a collision: the shrunken brick sits jammed against 'Sets for kids' and 'Buy 2 only for', which crowd into each other. Its price also hangs loose below the middle. A is slightly cleaner because nothing in it collides, and its ORDER NOW button is clearer.

Both are the same broken layout. The hero photo of praying hands is cropped into a thin, almost black L-shaped strip where the hands can't be recognised, so the key image is lost. The white cloud shapes sit on a white left half and vanish, which leaves about 40% of the canvas as empty dead space. The quote and attribution are readable and well set on the right. A differs only in a stray white cross clipped against the edge of the photo strip, while B's crosses are faint white-on-white marks in the empty area. Neither difference is better or worse.

A: the enlarged headline runs over the busy striped building photo ('the limit' sits right on the stripes), 'Sky is not' sticks out above the image strip, and there are empty white bands above and below, so it looks like the original banner pasted onto a taller canvas. B: the text mostly clears the photo, with only 'the' touching the image edge, but the headline breaks onto a third line with an orphaned 'us.' that spills below the strip, and the same dead white bands are still there. B is less broken because its text is more readable.

Both have the same structural flaw: the building photo no longer bleeds off the left edge. It sits inside a white strip of about 100 px and stops at a hard edge, with a faint panel edge on the right near x=625, so the layout reads as a shrunk, centred copy rather than a full-bleed banner. A keeps the headline closer to the original's scale and right anchor. B's headline is noticeably smaller and drifts inward, leaving more dead space on the right and weakening the main message, which makes it the slightly worse resize.

A keeps the '& Baby Toddler BEDDING' lockup intact but crams it and the thin image strip into the top quarter, leaving about 70% of the canvas as empty navy with stray dot grids floating in it; the headline is also small for a 300x600 format. B spreads the elements down the canvas and makes BEDDING large, but it splits the lockup so BEDDING floats far from 'Baby Toddler'. It also leaves the ampersand group pushed right and off-axis, and the dot grids crowd the image strip and the right edge; still, it reads top to bottom and uses the space better.

A: the hero image is cut down to a thin, unreadable sliver at the top. The '& Baby Toddler' lockup sits about 220px above 'BEDDING', so the brand phrase is split into fragments, and the dot patterns are scattered at random with no grid. Still, it reads top to bottom and the space is spread out reasonably. B: the ampersand and 'Baby Toddler' are jammed against the top edge and the image sliver, with no margin. 'BEDDING' floats mid-canvas, also split from the lockup, and the bottom ~45% is dead navy space, so B is more lopsided and cramped than A.

Both use the same broken layout. The CLAYTONI headline is blown up until it runs almost to the canvas edges and sits right on top of the busy illustration clusters, and the illustration strip is cut off flat at its bottom edge while the top third of the canvas is empty. A is slightly worse because CREATIVE AGENCY sits jammed against the cut-off bottom of the illustrations. B leaves the tagline a clear gap below them, which gives a little more breathing room.

The two share the same flawed layout. The symbol row is jammed against the top edge. The pink subcopy has a hard break that leaves 'CANNOT' alone on its own line. 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL.' is crammed into a narrow column. The event details are shrunk to about 5 px and can't be read. In A that detail text is also squeezed horizontally ('MAY,14TH' is mashed together) and nearly touches 'BECOME REAL.'. B keeps normal letter spacing and leaves a small gap, so it is slightly less broken.

Both are near-identical shrunk copies. The cat illustration is scaled down to a small strip. It loses the original's bottom-edge bleed and floats with a hard-cut base, the headline is small for a skyscraper, and the canvas has large empty purple areas. A sits high, leaving about 180 px of dead space at the bottom, so it reads lopsided. B centers the headline-and-cats group with roughly equal top and bottom margins, which makes it slightly more deliberate, though the dead space is still there.

Both get the hierarchy backwards: the subline 'food & drinks' is set much larger than the 'Order online' headline. Both also cram the headline into a tiny two-line stack and crop the packaging to unreadable slivers. A at least keeps a gap between the headline and 'food & drinks' and keeps a trace of the top rule. In B, 'online' butts right against 'food', so the two blocks read as one jammed cluster, and the rules are lost.

Both break the original's symmetric parallel couplet. The first PRAY is small and pushed off to the right of 'When Life Is Rough', while the second PRAY is huge and left-aligned, so the two halves no longer mirror each other. The vertical divider now runs down the left edge instead of separating the stanzas, and the text has a ragged, inconsistent scale against the rose. A leaves 'When Life Is Great' floating midway, cut off from its PRAY. B sits it nearer its PRAY, which groups the second stanza slightly better, but the layout is still incoherent.

A: the headline wraps into an orphaned 'us.' on a third line. The image and text sit in a thin middle band, with big empty bands above and below and dead space on the right, and 'the' just touches the image's tip. B: 'the limit for us.' runs well over the busy striped building photo, so the 'the' and 'limit' letterforms collide with the image and lose legibility. That is a clear unwanted overlap, and B also leaves large empty space below.

A: the '& Baby Toddler' lockup is jammed into the top-right corner. It collides with the blue photo strip and is nearly clipped at the canvas edge, while BEDDING floats mid-canvas over a huge empty bottom half, so it reads as cramped on top and dead below. B: there is no collision, but it is scattered. The '&' lockup sits off-axis to the right while BEDDING is centred, the dot patterns are fragments with the right-hand one clipped at the edge, the photo is shrunk to a thin sliver at the top, and the bottom is mostly dead space. Both are weak, but B is less broken.

Both break the design the same way. The white cloud graphic is pulled off the photo and floats as a near-invisible white shape on the white banner, so the original photo-plus-cloud composition is gone. 'JOIN OUR CHOIR!' is now tiny and smaller than 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!', which inverts the hierarchy. The photo is a small thumbnail stranded at the left, and the four elements spread across the width with no grouping. B is only marginally less bad: its photo and cloud are slightly larger, and its headline is a touch bigger.

Both have the same flaws. The hierarchy is inverted: the headline 'JOIN OUR CHOIR!' has shrunk to unreadable micro-text, and the subline 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!' has become the dominant element. The white cloud shape, which framed the text in the original, now floats on its own as a white-on-white blob with stray crosses. The photo is a small isolated box, and the canvas is broken into disconnected fragments with uneven gaps. B's photo and cloud are only a few pixels taller, so the two are effectively the same.

Both just shrink the landscape design into the portrait canvas, leaving big empty white bands above and below. The background pattern isn't extended and nothing is rearranged for the taller format. A also enlarges the white frame until it almost touches the left and right canvas edges, so the frame's margins drift from the original. B keeps the original inset frame and card proportions more faithfully, so it is marginally the better of two clearly unfinished resizes.

A keeps the original's structure: the headline sits on one line in the T's red crossbar, the stem bleeds off the bottom edge, and the text is readable. But it is a centred, shrunken copy that leaves large empty blue areas on the left and right, the text is small for the banner, and the right side of 'AGAINST CRUELTY' runs off the red stem onto blue. B wraps the headline so 'NOW!' sits alone on its own line, which breaks the original's one-line headline. Its T now floats with a gap above the bottom edge instead of bleeding off, the crossbar is cramped around the text, and it has the same dead blue side areas.

Both just stack the original's centred column into a wide banner with no left-to-right reflow, and in both the orange headline has broken off the column's centre axis and sits to the right of it, so the title no longer lines up with the dashes or the body copy. A is worse: the whole column sits left of centre (around x≈300), the right third of the canvas is empty apart from the stray headline, and the space is lopsided. B keeps the body column on the canvas centre, but its headline still sits about 80px right of that axis, close to the right edge, and the contact lines are tiny for this size.

A and B look the same. In both, the dashed divider has wrapped into a broken three-line stack of short dashes jammed between the headline and the body copy. The second divider floats above the teal line, which itself wraps awkwardly into three lines. The phone and website contact text is shrunk to an unreadable size and crammed against the right edge. 'creativity.' is left alone on its own line, and the columns are unevenly spaced. B's contact lines may be spaced very slightly further apart, but there is no real difference.

A and B are almost pixel-identical, and they share the same flaws. The brush-stroke shape that sits behind the title in the original has been moved up and floats alone above the cream jar, so it no longer frames the text. 'Spa Utopia' and the subtitle sit on top of the busy photo: they collide with the amber dropper at the left edge and the green leaves on the right. The subtitle 'Weekly SPA items review' is nearly as large as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy. The only difference is the shade of the floating stroke (slightly darker in A, paler in B), and it doesn't make either one better.

Both are the same crop: the product flat-lay that makes up the original's imagery is cropped down to fragments (a cut-off jar rim, a blurry glass, leaf tips), and the bottom third is empty pink. In both, the beige brush-stroke backing has come loose from the 'Spa Utopia' headline and floats above it as an odd blank shape, where in the original it sat behind the text. In A the stroke floats higher (it ends about 80px above the headline), so it reads as even more of an orphaned blob. B's stroke runs down almost to the headline, which keeps a little more of the original's text-on-stroke grouping.

Both are the same broken layout. The food photos have shrunk to tiny thumbnails sitting in background tiles. The orange frame and the plate illustration are scattered across the canvas as empty fragments. The frame is torn into separate pieces and the headline is cut off from the rest. A is marginally less bad because 'Cascadia RESTAURANT' stays together as a lockup, while B splits 'Cascadia' and 'RESTAURANT' far apart and breaks the brand mark.

A: the headline is large and fairly readable on the left, but it sits on the busy photo instead of the maroon panel. The X, O and line decorations are blown up into a cluster of meaningless shapes in the middle, and 'Join WADE team' is squeezed into a narrow maroon strip on the right, wrapped onto three lines. B: the maroon panel has drifted to the left, away from the text, so the white headline sits on the light grey table with weak contrast. 'Join WADE team' is tiny, crammed against the headline, and collides with the circle, while the X and line decorations are scattered at random.

Both crop the photo so tightly that the face is cut off above the nose and the eyes are lost, which makes the hero image hard to read and weakens fidelity to the original. In A, the lightbulb, atom and question-mark doodles sit right on the cheek and mouth, cluttering the face; that is clearly unintended. B moves the atom and question mark into the empty grey area next to the headline, where they read as decoration. Only B's lightbulb still clips the chin. B's headline block also sits better between its doodles, but the right-side molecule nearly touches 'WORKS?'.

A: the headline 'HOW IT WORKS?' is shrunk and collides with the man's smiling mouth, and the doodles (arrow, bulb, question mark, atom) are crushed into a row that sits on his face. The 'PODCAST WITH' subtitle floats far from the headline at the top right, and the oversized molecule takes over the right half, so the hierarchy and grouping are broken. B: the headline and subtitle stay together as a clear right-side block, as in the original. But the lightbulb doodle sits right on the man's nose and glasses, and the arrow lands on his ear. The photo is cropped tight, so the face is cut off at the left edge, and the molecule is cramped in the lower right.

Both crop the photo the same way, zooming in on the figs and losing the cake/tart, which weakens fidelity, and both float the wreath title in the dark upper-middle with lots of empty dark space on the left. A's wreath and title are a bit larger, so the headline is a stronger focal point, although its lower-right leaves brush the fig (the original also does this); B's lockup is smaller and clear of the fruit but undersized for a 768-wide banner, so the message reads weaker.

The two candidates look pixel-identical, and both share the same flaws. The orange-tinted backdrop that defined the brand is gone, leaving a dark purple photo with a mismatched orange block in the middle. The white frame shrinks to a meaningless fragment that collides with the 'n' of 'Pygmalion'. The fast-forward icon grows into a huge focal point that competes with the title. 'Music and lyrics by Leland Carroll' sits jammed against the top edge, and 'Richmond High School Theatre Presents' wraps into a cramped five-line column.

A: the headline re-wraps badly, leaving 'IS' alone on two lines (broken rag, orphans). The background is cropped to pixelated, unrecognisable fragments, and the colourful ART letterforms are mostly gone. B: the headline wraps cleanly, though 'IT IS' is a short line and the text block is crowded against the edge. B shares the same fidelity loss: blurry, upscaled fragments of 'RT' and 'A', a lot of beige and gold dead area at the bottom, and almost none of the original's multicolour identity survives.

Both candidates have the same core problems. The headline sits almost against the left canvas edge and wraps awkwardly: MODERN is left alone on its own line, and the blue/black colour split now reads as a ragged checkerboard. The photo is cropped down to a blurry, upscaled empty corridor, so the white furniture that defined the original is gone. The bottom third is dead space, and the translucent band behind the headline only partly covers it. In A, the black info box floats away from the blue box with a large, arbitrary gap, so the two related copy blocks read as scattered fragments. B keeps the two boxes stacked edge to edge with the same offset as the original, so its grouping and fidelity are better.

Both are the same layout and share the same flaws: the window graphic is pushed down-left and starts at x≈155, so it lines up with neither the headline's left edge nor any other element. The date/location block floats to the right of the window's top and is jammed against the headline, and the bottom-right quadrant is a large empty area, so the layout looks unbalanced rather than rearranged for the new shape. A puts the window very close to the bottom edge, with a heavier top margin above it. B has more even top and bottom margins but squeezes the window's arch almost into the headline, so B is only marginally better.

A keeps the reading order and the divider between the two phrases. The text is large and readable and the layout reads left to right, but the rose is clipped hard into a rectangle with visible straight edges, 'When Life Is Great' nearly touches the rose, and the right third of the canvas is dead space. B is broken: the order is jumbled (PRAY / Great / Rough / PRAY), so the message no longer makes sense; 'When Life Is Rough' is tiny and off-axis, the divider is stranded at the bottom-left corner beside the rose, and the text is small with lots of empty space.

Both candidates are unusable, and almost identical. In each one the headline 'We help choosing the right smartphone', the www.hosmart.au URL and the 'HO SMART' wordmark are gone, most likely white text on a white background. The blue brand panel is an empty wedge with nothing on it, the white-outline logo is barely visible on white, and the photo is shoved into a strip with the diagonal stripes cutting across the hand. The lower 60% of the canvas is empty. B is marginally less bad only because its logo sits closer to the photo, which leaves a slightly smaller dead gap than A's logo floating in the middle of nowhere.

Both versions keep the original's illustration strip as one band, without rearranging it, and enlarge the CLAYTONI headline until it runs straight over the busy figures at both edges. The graphics also stop at a hard flat cut along the bottom, with a dead navy band above. A is worse: the 'CREATIVE AGENCY' subtitle sits right on the bottom of the illustrations and the cut edge. B moves the subtitle below the strip onto plain background, so it reads cleanly, but the headline collisions and empty top band are still there.

A: the shrunken illustration strips collide with the bottom of 'CLAYTONI' and squeeze 'CREATIVE AGENCY' into a cramped two-line wrap between them, all crammed into the middle band with huge dead navy space above and below. B has no collisions, but the illustrations are shrunk to tiny side clusters with a big empty gap between them, 'CREATIVE AGENCY' is pushed far from its headline to the bottom, and large dead areas remain. It's still not shippable, but it's cleaner than A.

A: the body copy, dividers and contact lines are centred on the canvas, but the orange 'Traditional Ceramics Workshop' headline sits about 170px right of that axis, so the headline no longer lines up with anything. It is also still the square's vertical stack squeezed into a banner, with tiny contact text and no left-to-right layout. B has the same off-axis headline, and on top of that the whole stack drifts left of centre (body axis around x=300), leaving a dead empty right third and an obviously lopsided canvas, so it is worse.

Both have the same flaws. The taupe brush-stroke panel that sat behind the title is now orphaned above the text as a meaningless grey shape. 'Spa Utopia' and the subtitle now sit over a busy image, colliding with the amber dropper on the left and the green leaves and capsule on the right. The subtitle is set almost as large as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy, and it runs nearly edge to edge. B is marginally worse because its headline and subtitle are jammed tighter, so Utopia's descenders almost touch 'Weekly'. A leaves slightly more breathing room.

A keeps a clean right-side text column (headline over subtitle, good hierarchy) and a sensible photo crop, but the lightbulb doodle lands right on the man's nose and glasses, and the arrow cuts across his cheek, which are unwanted collisions on the face. In B the 'HOW IT WORKS?' headline sits over his mouth and chin, the doodles (arrow, bulb, question mark, atom) are jammed into one overlapping row across his face, and the subtitle is tiny and stranded in the top-right corner, far from its headline. That breaks hierarchy, grouping and the rule against text over a busy image.

Both share the same flaws: the headline wraps awkwardly (MODERN alone on a line, then FURNITURE DESIGN, then FESTIVAL), runs almost into the left canvas edge, and sits on the busy photo; the bottom third is dead image space. A keeps the blue and black boxes interlocked as one stacked group, as in the original. B leaves an arbitrary gap between them, so the photo shows through, the two boxes read as separate fragments, and the cluster ends up lower and less balanced.

A scrambles the message: the order reads PRAY / When Life Is Great / When Life Is Rough / PRAY. 'When Life Is Rough' is smaller and left-offset, the divider line is left alone at the bottom-left beside the rose, and the rose is cropped into a hard rectangle. B keeps the original reading order, the divider and the type hierarchy at a legible size. But the rose is cropped into a visible rectangle with its stem cut off, the text block is tight to the left edge while about 180 px of dead space sits to the right of the rose, and the two halves of the layout feel crammed together.

A keeps GET A GIFT as the dominant element and splits brand, headline and offer into sensible banner columns, but the dashed divider rules are scattered loose in the left column, the LYGOM CAFE logo and www.lygom.se are tiny, and the left-hand stack is cramped against the canvas edge. B reverses the hierarchy: 'with your next cup of coffee' is set huge, in white, directly over the busy sweater/mug photo (unwanted collision, poor legibility), while the headline GET A GIFT shrinks to a minor label. The gift icons are oversized, 'Only this Christmas' and the stars sit on the photo, and two full-width dashed lines run across the bottom for no reason, so B is unusable.

Both pull the text off the red T, so the original's signature layering (headline sitting on the red bar) is lost, and the T becomes a loose decorative shape on the right with a dead gap in the middle. A's headline is larger and anchored to a clean left margin, and its T fills the height with tight but even top and bottom margins. B's headline is noticeably smaller and floats in from the left with no clear grid, its T is shrunk, and the composition feels underscaled with more empty blue.

A: the orange headline is pushed to the right edge, far off the centred axis that every other element shares, so the top of the layout looks lopsided and broken. B: the headline is roughly back on the centre axis, but the column is still a little ragged (the headline, dividers, teal line and contact lines are all a few pixels off a true centre). Both just stretch the square layout into a narrow centred strip, leaving big empty bands on each side. The headline is too small to anchor a wide banner, and the contact fine print is tiny.

Both lose the dropper bottles and capsules, and both leave the brush-stroke backing floating empty in the middle with the title moved below it. That breaks the original's text-on-stroke lockup, and in both the subtitle wraps so that 'review' sits alone on the last line. B is slightly worse: 'Spa Utopia' crowds against the bottom of the glass jar, and about 40% of the canvas at the bottom is dead space. A keeps the headline clear of the jar, but its bottom fifth is still empty.

Both fall apart the same way. The two food photos are shrunk to thumbnail-sized crops inside their panels, which leaves big empty peach and pattern blocks, and the white frame is left as an empty box. The flourish dividers float between elements as stray arrows, the wrapped 'New pasta menu' headline is crowded against the left edge, and the brand block on the right is too small to read. B's only difference is slightly looser spacing in 'RESTAURANT' and the URL, so neither is the better resize.

Both break the design the same way. The background panels, frame and pattern are scattered as separate pieces. The photos shrink to tiny thumbnails cropped inside the peach and pattern blocks, with empty photo frames below them. The orange frame stands empty, and the divider flourishes float loose in the strip. A at least keeps 'Cascadia RESTAURANT' together as one lockup, while B splits 'Cascadia' and 'RESTAURANT' far apart, which further damages the brand.

A: the full-height maroon panel keeps the original's centred-panel structure and holds the text block cleanly. But 'MARKETING' runs almost to the panel's edges, 'Join WADE team' has wide, loose word gaps, and the X, slash and circle accents now sit on the busy photo (the X lands on the hands) instead of framing the panel. B: the panel is narrower and stops at an arbitrary height short of the bottom edge, so it looks like a floating, cut-off box. 'MARKETING' nearly touches both sides of the panel, there is a lopsided gap between 'WADE' and 'team', and the corner accents are scattered over the photo just as in A.

A breaks the text group: the 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow is stranded at the very top while the headline sits on the bottom edge. That reverses the reading order, and the confetti is shrunk into a thin band, leaving big dead gaps between the bands. B keeps the headline and subhead together in the middle, but the eyebrow has moved below the headline at a size that nearly competes with it. B's owls are also tiny at the bottom, the confetti is squeezed into a band at the top, and large empty areas are left above and below.

Both share the same broken layout. The original's diamond photo mosaic is reduced to one small rectangular photo plus an empty wireframe of diamond outlines in the top right, and an orphaned rule sits under it. The two brown diamonds float on their own, the body copy is tiny, and the URL is crammed against the right edge. A sits close to the headline and roughly lines up with the photo's left edge, so headline and copy read as one group. B floats the body copy out into the middle, where it lines up with nothing and leaves a dead gap next to the headline.

Both lose the white panel and turn the full-bleed grey/blue/red stripes into thin, detached bars. All the copy shrinks to an unreadable few pixels ($49.99 is the only legible line) and floats on blank white with a big dead gap between it and the stripes. A pushes the text block to the far right edge, leaving an empty left margin and middle. B parks the stripes at the left edge and centres the text, leaving the right third dead, and its letter spacing breaks down ('COFFEEMUGS', 'TRAVELMUGS'). A is marginally less broken.

The two are nearly identical. Both make the $49.99 price huge but shrink 'for all drinkware on' to a tiny three-line stack. Both keep the URL vertical at microscopic size, so it can't be read. Both push the product list against the right edge, leave a large dead gap in the middle, and lose the original's white card and full-height colour stripes. Those are reduced to a small grey and blue/red sliver on the left. The only visible difference is that B's left stripe block runs a few pixels taller, which doesn't matter.

A: the banner opens with the dates block, which wraps badly ('JUNE / 8-24 JULY 2-18 / AUGUST / 4-20') and is jammed against the left edge, so the reading order runs dates → image → headline → invitation. The cross butts into the illustration, and all the secondary copy is unreadably small at this size. B has the same tiny, badly wrapped invitation and dates, crammed against both canvas edges, and the invitation reads before the headline. But it ends on the dates, so its order (invitation → headline → image → details) is slightly more logical, and the cross/worship line sits cleanly under the headline.

Both share the same flaws: the background is cropped to a blurry, washed-out fragment of the interior with no recognisable furniture, so the original's key imagery is effectively lost. 'COPENHAGEN' runs almost to the right canvas edge, the headline sits over busy shelving behind 'FURNITURE/DESIGN', and the info boxes don't share the headline's left edge. A also floats the black box apart from the blue one with a loose gap near the bottom, which scatters the info group. B keeps the two boxes stacked and offset as in the original, so it groups and reads better, though it leaves a slightly larger empty band at the bottom.

The two are almost identical and share the same flaws. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow is pulled away from the headline and stranded at the far left, which breaks the grouping and reading order. 'KIDS DIRTHDAY PARTIES' sits almost against the top and bottom edges. Both owls are shrunk to small icons, and the hanging owl is cropped and wedged next to the headline while confetti crowds the text. A's eyebrow is slightly larger and easier to read; B's is smaller and feels even more cut off from the headline, so A wins by a hair.

Both are letterboxed: the patterned background band stops roughly 85px from the top and bottom, leaving flat white bars so the image reads as a shrunk copy, not a resize, and the pattern's edges are hard-cropped. A keeps more of the triangle and squiggle art visible around a centred panel, and its gold keyline frame stays close to the original. B stretches the dark panel to about 73% of the width, which covers most of the brand pattern and leaves the headline floating in an oversized empty box.

A splits the 'HOHOHO AGENCY' wordmark with a strip of shrunken shapes squeezed into a thin band between the two words. 'Office Secret Santa' is wrapped onto three cramped lines jammed against the blue C and triangle, and there is dead space at the top. B keeps the text together as one clean, readable block, but it reverses the brand order, putting HOHOHO below AGENCY and the tagline. Its lower half is a loose scatter of graphics, including cut-off semicircles and a gold cross overlapping a black triangle, with no clear grid.

A cuts the photo down to a short strip hanging from the top edge. The praying hands, the key image, are cropped almost entirely away, the crosses float faintly on white outside the photo, and the cloud outlines on the left are ghostly white-on-white shapes in a big dead area. B keeps more of the hands and the cross, but its white text panel bites a hard rectangular notch out of the photo, the column is pinned to the centre while the left third is empty except for the invisible cloud outlines, and the quote sits off-axis from the image. Both are poor; B is slightly better because more of the original imagery survives.

Both use the same broken layout. The headline panel and the thin yellow frame sit on the left, with the bottom half of the frame left empty. The photo is cut off from them as a small inset on the right. Stray yellow tick marks float in white space and on the photo's edge, and a yellow bar is cropped at the top. The original's layered headline-over-photo design is lost. B's photo is slightly larger but sits closer to the right edge, so neither one is meaningfully better.

Both have the same flaws. The building photo, the original's key image, is shrunk to a tiny cropped sliver on the left edge, and a faint light band from its background runs behind the headline. The headline breaks into short, awkward lines ('not' / 'the' alone). The rest of the canvas is mostly empty white. A is worse: its smaller headline sits low, under a large dead area at the top. B's slightly larger headline fills the frame a little better, but the stranded image and band are still there.

A keeps the '& Baby Toddler' logo and 'BEDDING' together on one baseline as the original lockup, but everything sits in the top 35%. The bottom ~60% of the canvas is empty navy, and the dot clusters are scattered at random, so the layout is badly lopsided. B has the same empty bottom and also breaks the brand lockup: 'BEDDING' drops below the logo and floats off to the right with no shared alignment. Its stray dot grid on the right edge makes the arrangement look even more arbitrary.

Both are nearly the same layout. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow is split off from its headline and left floating alone in the empty left third, while the two-line headline is squeezed between the top and bottom edges. On the right, the owl and confetti crowd the headline, and the owl figures are too small to read as the key imagery. B sets the stray eyebrow a little further in, so it is less pinned to the left edge and the left side is slightly less lopsided. A's eyebrow hugs the edge.

A: the photo is a narrow strip down the middle, and a white text panel cuts a hard rectangle into its lower right, so the quote and the image collide awkwardly. The cloud shape is white on a white background, so it is invisible and only stray outlines show; the left third is dead, and the cross glyphs sit on the hands. B: the photo is cropped to a small square that loses most of the hands, and a cross glyph floats loose outside the photo. The cloud is again invisible white on white, and the left side is empty. Still, the quote and author sit cleanly on white with no collision, so B is the less broken of the two.

Both break the design the same way. The frame is split from the photo: the headline card sits alone in a mostly empty left frame, with dead space under it. The photo is a small, unrelated tile on the right, and the gold accent dashes have come loose: they float in empty space and two land on the photo's top edge. The top yellow bar is pushed off-centre at the right. A puts its frame tight to the left edge and its photo nearly against the right edge, so it feels more cramped. B's margins are slightly more even, but its photo is smaller and the frame is just as empty, so the two are close.

Both break the search-bar motif: the magnifier icon has slid out of its box and floats to the right, leaving an empty divided cell. The photo also floats in a white gutter that doesn't line up with the orange panel. In A, the panel and photo fill most of the height. B is the same layout with a thicker dead white strip under the panel and photo, which reads as cropped and unbalanced, so A is slightly less bad.

A shrinks both owls to tiny icons squeezed beside the headline. It strands 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' about 300px above its headline, packs the confetti into a thin middle band, and leaves large dead white areas at the top and bottom, so the hero imagery becomes trivial. B keeps the owls large and the headline big and dominant with a clear top-to-bottom flow, but the eyebrow still sits far from the headline at the top, the confetti is squashed into a dense strip, and the owls are not aligned to the left text edge.

A: the confetti is shrunk into a tiny, meaningless cluster in the middle-left, and the owls float alone at mid-right. The headline is pushed small into the bottom-right corner, far from its 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow, which leaves large dead areas and a broken reading order. B: the confetti keeps its scale across the top and the headline is large and dominant, with the owls grouped beside it. However, the owls are shrunk to tiny props, the eyebrow sits stranded at the top far from the headline, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty.

A shrinks the crowd illustration into a small strip in the top-left, leaving dead white space beside it and losing the key image. Its quote breaks badly, with an orphaned 'OF THOUGHTFUL' line and a ragged 'THE WORLD; INDEED,', and the attribution needlessly wraps onto two lines. B keeps the crowd large and full-width across the top, so it stays faithful to the original. It shares the same awkward forced breaks ('OF THOUGHTFUL' orphan), and its text block and one-line attribution sit cramped against the left, right and bottom edges with almost no margin.

A: the crowd illustration shrinks to an unrecognisable sliver on the left. The red Margaret Mead attribution becomes illegible grey specks stranded under the image, far from the quote it belongs to, and the quote's text is tiny with a large dead gap on the right. B has the same failures, with the attribution again a speck under the image and cut off from the quote, but the quote is also jammed against the left canvas edge and the original's image-then-quote order is reversed, so A is slightly less bad.

Both reduce the crowd illustration, the original's main image, to a thin strip of tiny figures. Both also wrap the quote into a narrow column whose long lines (THOUGHTFUL, COMMITTED, CAN CHANGE) almost touch the right edge, and both leave a dead white band at the bottom. A is slightly better because its crowd bleeds off the top edge like the original's. B's crowd is an even smaller inset strip with odd white space above it and a ragged crop.

Both pull the quote out of the floral frame, which now shows the stock 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION / HAND DRAWN ELEMENTS' placeholder text, so the original's quote-inside-frame concept is broken and the frame looks like an unrelated thumbnail. A wraps the attribution to 'CAROLYN / MURPHY', jammed right under 'MAKEUP.', and leaves 'MEN' alone on the first line. B leaves 'JUST' orphaned on its own line, and its one-line 'CAROLYN MURPHY' runs almost edge to edge with no margin, so A is marginally cleaner.

A breaks the reading order: the pink subhead sits above the headline at the top right, with bad breaks ('YOU CANNOT' / 'VIRTUAL' orphaned). 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL' is squeezed into a one-word-per-line column, and the event body copy is microscopic and unreadable. B is a sensible two-column banner: the symbols sit on the left and the text stack on the right keeps the original order and hierarchy. But the pink square nearly touches the subhead's left edge, the URL is centred while the rest of the text is left-aligned, and the large empty area above and below the shrunken symbols makes the left side feel unanchored.

Both are broken the same way: the forest background stays a narrow centred strip on a white banner, so the white headline, subhead and body copy that fall outside it disappear, and the text inside it is cut off mid-word. The 'March 21' text and the cream divider lines float in empty white space. A keeps slightly more of the headline ('Devoted / al Day / s') while B cuts it to 'oted / Day' and keeps more body copy, so A is marginally less bad; neither is usable.

A is unusable: the forest background is a narrow centre strip, the white headline sits on the white canvas and can't be seen (only stray 'd' and 'y' glyphs show), and the subline, quote and URL are clipped at the strip edges, with divider lines floating at the bottom. B is just the portrait original shrunk into the middle of the banner, with large empty white areas on both sides. Its headline runs past the strip ('Devoted', 'Day' clipped), the body text is too small to read, and the divider lines have broken off to the far right, but at least it still reads as the same design.

Both are unusable. The forest background was not stretched to the landscape canvas, so it fills only a narrow centre strip, and the white headline runs off it onto the white side areas, where it disappears ('Event Devo… ernational D… f Forests'). A also clips the subtitle ('…ration & Forest clea…') and leaves a stray divider line floating on the white area at the right. B is worse: it drops the subtitle, both rules and all the body copy, leaves an orphaned divider line at the top left, and puts the date on top of the busy treeline. So A keeps slightly more of the message.

In A the hierarchy is flipped: the headline 'Order online' shrinks until it is smaller than the 'food & drinks' subline, which floats far to the right and runs over the kraft box, so text sits on a busy image. The rules also no longer frame the text block. B has every A flaw and adds a direct collision: the headline jams against 'food & drinks', the subline covers the box image even more heavily, and the rules sit away from the type.

A: 'Order online' is jammed right up against 'food & drinks', so they read as one tangled lockup. The subhead is now bigger than the headline, it runs onto the kraft boxes ('drinks' sits on the busy image), and one rule floats stranded on the box photo. B: the headline gets its own space on the left, but the hierarchy is still upside down (the small headline loses to the big subhead), 'drinks' still collides with the box image, the orphaned rule still floats on the photo, and the two text pieces are scattered with no shared alignment.

Both put the photo in a short band that doesn't fill the taller canvas, so it has hard top and bottom edges with empty white strips above and below. Both also push the headline left so 'the limit' sits on the busy striped building, which the original avoided. A is worse: its larger text starts further left (~x160), so 'the' and 'l' sit fully on the photo and the headline crowds the right edge. B's slightly smaller headline overlaps the image less and has a bit more right margin, but still collides with the photo.

A and B look pixel-identical, and both are unusable. In each, the blue background is gone and only a small blue slanted bar is left floating near the top of a mostly white canvas. The headline, the URL and the 'HO SMART' wordmark are all missing. The hand-and-phone photo has shrunk to a thin sliver, and the white device-outline logo sits on white, so it barely shows and collides with the photo strip.

Both are almost the same. In each, the crowd illustration that carried the original has shrunk to a thin strip of tiny figures, so the key image is lost. The quote is broken into 12 short lines with awkward breaks ('INDEED,' left alone on its own line, a ragged right edge). 'THOUGHTFUL' and 'CHANGE' run almost to the right edge, and empty space is left at the bottom. A also floats its crowd strip under an odd top gap, which makes it look like a pasted thumbnail. B runs its crowd strip off the top edge the way the original does, so it is slightly closer to the original, but its strip is just as small.

Both are unusable: the forest background stays a narrow centred strip and leaves white bands on both sides, so the white headline runs off it onto white and becomes illegible ('…Event Devot / …rnational Da'). A also drops the subhead, both dividers, the quote and the URL, and leaves a stray divider line top-left. B is slightly worse: 'March 21' sits in cream on the pale sky with almost no contrast, the subhead is cut off at both ends ('…ration & Forest clea…'), a divider floats outside the background on the right, and the quote and URL are still missing.
